reasoning: For each candidate I mapped its reported events onto the seven known causal chains, then scored it on: (1) whether the events fall in the chain's correct temporal order (any event that is chronologically downstream of a later-stage event is a strong 'scrambled' red flag, e.g. C-9 which has all six supply-chain stages present but in near-random order, and C-4 whose audit_finding is reported after the regulatory_notice that should follow it); (2) how much of a single causal chain is actually covered by first_seen_day, rewarding multi-stage progressions over one or two isolated events that could just be coincidence (C-13, C-53, C-7 only cover 2-3 non-adjacent stages); (3) breadth of genuine cross-organisational corroboration via independent_sources, distinct_sites and distinct_regions, discounting cases where total_reports vastly exceeds independent_sources (duplicated chatter re-counted as corroboration, e.g. C-52, C-1, C-10); (4) whether the candidate's events cleanly belong to one chain versus being a grab-bag spanning many unrelated chains, which is pure coincidence (C-16 touches six different chains at once); and (5) entity-level contradiction_count and staleness (an incomplete, narrowly-sourced, or long-dormant chain, e.g. C-28's full but single-site chain, or C-8's chain that went quiet after day ~99, reads as routine/local/resolved rather than an active cross-org risk). The 15 candidates escalated as genuine all show a properly time-ordered, uncontradicted subsequence of a real causal chain corroborated by several independent sources across at least ~2.5 distinct regions on average, with no evidence of duplicate-chatter inflation or multi-chain coincidence — the combination the task describes as a real causal progression actually underway.
